result.answer: That is already how this case ran. The demo bed-management system behind Downstream Out is set to hold only the patient's current placement (W1 describes that setting). The transfer to WARD-B, bay 2 bed 04, at 09:20 UTC failed because the system was unavailable. The system has no record of receiving it. A later transfer to WARD-C, bay BAY1-07, at 09:45 UTC was accepted (version 2). So the current placement is already right. Shutter closed the case as overtaken and sent nothing. Resending the WARD-B transfer would move the patient back to a ward they had left. The only gap is that the short WARD-B stay is missing from the history. The specialists agree on the outcome but look at it from different sides. Conformance says the message itself was fine and was not the cause. Encounter says the message's intent no longer holds. Impact says resending would do harm, but Shutter cannot tell from this case whether any other system needs the WARD-B stay. The only alternative in the evidence goes the other way: keeping a full movement history. Under that setting the case would go to a person (W1). No change is needed for what you asked.

perspectives.view: The message is a valid 2.5.1 transfer that matches the route. The failure was the receiver being unavailable, not the content. Site-specific rules are not fully checked. The setting decides the outcome, not the message.

The intent no longer holds. The patient is in WARD-C after the later 09:45 UTC transfer, so resending WARD-B would be wrong. The evidence shows the order of the messages, not whether the patient actually stayed in WARD-B.
With current placement only, nothing is lost by sending nothing, and resending would show the wrong location. It is unknown whether any other system needs the missing WARD-B stay.
